claims.text: The proposed material is a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
The relevant alloy can be represented by a WxTaTiVCr composition.
The initial alloy has uncontrolled nanoprecipitate formation.
Stepwise adjustment of spark-plasma-sintering temperatures can produce a high density of uniform coherent nanoprecipitates.
A high density of homogeneously distributed coherent nanoprecipitates facilitates continuous dislocation transmission at high temperature.
Coherent, homogeneously distributed precipitates mitigate dislocation pile-up during plastic deformation.
Dislocation transmission across coherent interfaces relieves stress concentrations and delays crack initiation.
Controlled coherent nanoprecipitates enhance high-temperature plastic strain.
Controlled coherent nanoprecipitates enhance toughness under fusion plasma-facing conditions.
The coherent nanoprecipitates are situated within a BCC matrix.
The coherent nanoprecipitates provide low-energy interfaces.
Optimized nanoprecipitate formation will increase toughness at 800 °C relative to an uncontrolled baseline.
Optimized nanoprecipitate formation will produce more homogeneous and less localized plastic deformation at 800 °C.
Lack of precipitate-control processing produces inhomogeneous and less coherent precipitates in the baseline.
Mechanical testing at approximately 800 °C is representative of fusion plasma-facing environments.
The mechanism requires precipitate coherence and a sufficiently uniform precipitate distribution.
Lattice-parameter relationships that produce incoherent precipitates can prevent the proposed mechanism.
The mechanism may not apply in significantly different temperature regimes.
A controlled comparison should use an optimized coherent-precipitate set and a standard-processing baseline, with TEM used to characterize the mediator.
Failure to obtain significantly higher toughness and more uniform deformation in the optimized samples is specified as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The optimized group is defined as having achieved a uniform coherent-precipitate structure, but the rule also treats finding no TEM difference between groups as falsification. No mediator difference would instead indicate failure of the intervention or manipulation check, not falsification of the proposed mediator-to-outcome mechanism.
